method: Started from about 2,000 priced Kalshi legs in the next 36 hours. Kept legs priced 30–85¢ with edge of about −2.5 or better and no flags, one per game, and checked them against today's 134 newly collected expert picks, injury and goalie news, and Polymarket top-trader positions. The later dump returned no top-trader data, so sharp figures come from the same script's run about 40 minutes earlier. A leg stayed only if at least two of (top traders, a published pick or model, concrete news) agreed and nothing disagreed. Dropped for conflicts: the Spurs spread (Dimers' model is on Pistons +8.5) and the Spurs-Pistons Under (three picks, but top traders are $1.9k against); the Knicks (top traders $6.6k on Toronto, three outlets on Raptors +2.5 to +3.5); the Senators (two picks, but $13k of top-trader money against Ottawa's puck line); Clippers-Jazz (SI on Utah +6.5, top traders against the Clippers); Ducks vs Blues on the side (two picks on Anaheim, $3.8k of top-trader money on St. Louis); Ball State +10.5/+11.5 (three picks, but PFN lays -11.5 with Ohio); Illinois-Duke and Miami (OH)-Kent State (experts split); and Akron-UMass (UMass QB Watson's ankle injury, small money against). Bruins moneyline (edge −2.75) was swapped for Bruins +1.5. Wednesday NBA and NHL previews weren't published yet, so the only Wednesday leg is the MAC game, which is placed last so it fills the ladder after Tuesday's games start.
honest: Every leg costs slightly more than its fair price (edge about −0.8 to −2.4¢ each), so expected return is slightly negative, and it gets worse with each leg you add.

ladder.label: Toronto Maple Leafs
ladder.why: Three published picks take Toronto: Last Word On Hockey (Leafs 3-2), Bettors Insider (Leafs 4-3) and Covers' Neil Parker (model about 71%). Toronto's power play is 6th (26.7%) against Chicago's 30th (14.3%), and Toronto has the better 5-on-5 expected goals. Polymarket's top sports traders hold about $34.5k on Toronto and none on Chicago.

sources.name: Last Word On Hockey / Braden Morrison (Leafs ML)

ladder.game: Eastern Michigan Eagles @ Western Michigan Broncos
ladder.label: Western Michigan Broncos −13.5
ladder.why: Covers (Colby Marchio), Pickswise (Chad Hartsock) and Pro Football Network (Jason Katz) all lay -14.5 with Western Michigan, and no one we found takes Eastern Michigan. EMU's defense allows nearly 30 points, 6.1 yards a play and 400+ yards a game, and it gives up the second-most explosive runs in the MAC to a WMU offense that runs on 62% of plays. Pickswise also notes that EMU's offense has stalled without QB Noah Kim, whose status is up in the air.

ladder.label: Michigan State Spartans
ladder.why: SI's Peter Dewey lays -3.5 with Michigan State, and BetMGM's model gives the Spartans 61.9% to win. Michigan State ranks 10th in adjusted offense and 5th in adjusted defense, while Tennessee (36th on KenPom) is outside the top 25 in both. The Spartans beat Duke last week, and Jeremy Fears Jr. averages 16.8 points and 10.0 assists.

ladder.label: Over 6.5
ladder.why: SI's Ryan Gilbert and TheSpread's Paul Elliot both take Over 6.5. Anaheim has gone over in 14 of 21 games, including 10 of its last 11, and its games average about 7.4 goals. St. Louis may start Jordan Binnington (4.27 GAA, .851 SV%), and Hofer allowed four goals last time out. No published pick takes the Under.

ladder.label: Tampa Bay Lightning
ladder.why: Last Word On Hockey predicts Lightning 5-3, and SportsBettingDime's Michael Schwartz backs Tampa Bay to win in regulation. Tampa is 13-5-2 and 8-1-0 at home, Washington allowed 12 goals in two losses to New Jersey, and Vasilevskiy is expected in net. The risk is injuries: Cirelli and Cernak missed the last game and Point has been out for three. Top-trader money is small but on Tampa ($191 for, $0 against).

sources.name: Last Word On Hockey / Joe Rendace (Lightning)

ladder.label: Over 218.5
ladder.why: TheRx (Over 219.5) and Sports Mole (Over 218.5) both take the Over. The Lakers score 122.8 a game and Charlotte allows 119.2, and the Lakers are 10-4 to the Over. Top-trader money is roughly even ($3.3k for, $3.0k against), and no published pick takes the Under.

ladder.label: San Antonio Spurs
ladder.why: Covers' Geoff Clark takes the Spurs moneyline, and FanDuel Research, Lineups, Sports Mole and TheRx all lay about -9.5. San Antonio is on a 12-game win streak, and Detroit is without starting center Jalen Duren (and Duncan Robinson and Ron Holland II) against Wembanyama. Top traders hold about $66.6k on the Spurs against $8.5k.

ladder.label: Boston Bruins +1.5
ladder.why: SI (Ryan Gilbert), Bettors Insider (Jessica Stone) and numberFire's model (71.3%) all take Boston on the moneyline; this leg only needs Boston not to lose by 2+. The Kings have lost four straight and are 5-11-2, while Boston is 8-3-0 at home after two days' rest. Top-trader money on the moneyline leans Boston ($1.5k for, $0.3k against).

ladder.label: Buffalo Bulls −1.5
ladder.why: VSiN's Adam Burke takes Buffalo -2.5 on Wednesday. Central Michigan is down to backup QB Jadyn Glasser after Angel Flores was hurt. Buffalo allows 3.95 yards a carry in MAC play against CMU's 4.63, and SP+ ranks Buffalo's special teams 66th and CMU's 126th. No published pick takes Central Michigan.
